lessons.title: તે ગુજરાતી બોલે છે — the present, for someone else
lessons.gloss: the present for he, she and familiar you: the stem takes -e, and the copula is che

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to change, the last verb of the A1 words. Then the first sentence you ever built about yourself.

segments.instruction: badalvũ, then hũ gujarātī bolũ chũ

segments.text: That sentence has three working pieces: the stem બોલ- (speak), the ending -ું that says I, and છું, the copula that agrees with I. Change the person and two of the three pieces move.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: one ending for he, she and તું

segments.text: તે ગુજરાતી બોલે છે. — te gujarātī bole che. — He speaks Gujarati. She speaks Gujarati.
The stem stays બોલ-. The person ending becomes -ે, and the copula becomes છે, the commonest word in this book. The familiar you takes the very same pair:
તું ગુજરાતી બોલે છે. — tũ gujarātī bole che. — You speak Gujarati.

utterances: who: હું. verb: બોલું. copula: છું.
who: તું, તે. verb: બોલે. copula: છે.

segments.text: તું and તે share one verb form, so only the pronoun in front tells them apart. જવું bends its stem a little and keeps the idea: તે જાય છે, she goes.

segments.source: [YOU SAY: *hũ gujarātī bolũ chũ*, then *te gujarātī bole che*]

segments.text: Which two pieces change when I speak becomes she speaks? (The ending -ું becomes -ે, and છું becomes છે.) Which pronoun shares her verb form? (તું, the familiar you.)

lessons.title: તેઓ (teo) — they
lessons.gloss: they; also he or she, said with respect

segments.text: Before the new one: say she speaks Gujarati. Then the pronoun on its own, તે, the word for anyone who is not here.
તેઓ (teo) — "they".
It is તે with -ઓ (o) on the end. તે names one person who is not here; તેઓ (teo) names more than one.
તેઓ ગુજરાતી બોલે છે. — teo gujarātī bole che. — They speak Gujarati.
The verb does not move: બોલે છે serves તેઓ (teo) exactly as it serves તે. In the present, he, she, familiar you and they all meet on -ે છે.
તેઓ (teo) does a second job. Said of one person, it is a respectful he or she: a teacher, a grandparent, a guest. So તેઓ (teo) અહીં છે is they are here, or he is here, said with respect.
તેઓ (teo) is તે plus -ઓ (o), the ending Gujarati nouns take for "more than one". તે continues the old Sanskrit demonstrative stem ta-, whose plural te already meant "they" (CDIAL 5612).
One more pronoun, and the present now has four people on one ending.

segments.instruction: teo
તેઓ અહીં રહે છે — teo ahī̃ rahe che, they live here
segments.source: [YOU SAY: **તેઓ અહીં રહે છે** — *teo ahī̃ rahe che*, they live here]

lessons.gloss: the standing vowel o, the letter that ends તેઓ

segments.instruction: say they — R1, one lesson back
say the standing vowel આ, and the sign ો that gives a consonant its o
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say the standing vowel **આ**, and the sign **ો** that gives a consonant its *o*]

segments.text: તેઓ (teo) ends on a vowel that stands alone. After a consonant, o is a sign: તો, જો. At the start of a syllable there is no consonant to carry it, so o needs a letter of its own.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: આ with an arc above

segments.text: ઓ (o) is built on આ. Keep the whole of આ, the body and its stems on the right, and set one high arc over the top.

utterances: letter: આ. sound: ā. what it is made of: the body and its stems.
letter: ઓ. sound: o. what it is made of: આ, then a high arc.

segments.text: ઓ — o.

Keep ઓ (o) visible. Write the joined body of આ first: the open curve on the left, the broad lower body, the small shoulder and arch. Lift, and bring the first stem down the right side to its foot. Lift again and bring the trailing stem down beside it. Lift a last time and sweep the high arc from left to right over the top. Four movements, three lifts.
The arc sits high and clear of the stems. Without it the letter reads આ.
Finger-trace ઓ (o) once, then air-trace it once. Notice the body of આ, the two stems, and the arc that rides above them.
Copy visible ઓ (o) once. Compare only two things: are both stems there, and does the arc clear their tops? Repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write the standing vowel o once. Uncover ઓ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write the standing vowel o from memory.

feedback.correct: ઓ — the body of આ, two stems, and the high arc.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at ઓ, hide it, and repair only the landmark that differs.

lessons.title: અમે ગુજરાતી બોલીએ છીએ — the present for we, and for you
lessons.gloss: the present for we and for respectful you: -īe chīe, and -o cho

segments.text: Say they speak Gujarati. Then the two words for we: અમે, which leaves the listener out, and આપણે, which takes the listener in.

segments.instruction: teo gujarātī bole che; ame, āpṇe
ઓ (o) once from memory

segments.text: અમે ગુજરાતી બોલીએ છીએ. — ame gujarātī bolīe chīe. — We speak Gujarati.

The ending is -ીએ, and the copula has a form you have not met before: છીએ (chīe). Both finish on the same -ીએ, so the sentence chimes. આપણે takes the same pair: આપણે ગુજરાતી બોલીએ છીએ, we (you and I) speak Gujarati.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: respectful you

segments.text: તમે કેમ છો? has carried છો since the second day. The verb beside તમે takes the matching -ો:
તમે ગુજરાતી બોલો છો. — tame gujarātī bolo cho. — You speak Gujarati.
The present endings for one person:

utterances: who: હું. verb: બોલું. copula: છું.
who: તું, તે. verb: બોલે. copula: છે.

segments.text: And for more than one, or for respect:

utterances: who: અમે, આપણે. verb: બોલીએ. copula: છીએ.
who: તમે. verb: બોલો. copula: છો.
who: તેઓ (teo). verb: બોલે. copula: છે.

અમે અહીં રહીએ છીએ — ame ahī̃ rahīe chīe, we live here

segments.text: Which copula ends on the same sound as its verb for we? (છીએ, after -ીએ.) Which ending goes with તમે? (-ો, then છો.)

lessons.title: હું નથી બોલતો — saying not about what people do
lessons.gloss: saying that someone does not do something: nathī, and the verb in -to, -tī or -tā

segments.text: Say we speak Gujarati and you speak Gujarati. Then the repair sentence from long ago: સમજતો નથી, I do not understand.
That sentence already holds the whole negative. Here is how it is built.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: નથી takes the copula's place

segments.text: હું ગુજરાતી નથી બોલતો. — hũ gujarātī nathī bolto. — I don't speak Gujarati.
Two changes, and only two:
છું goes, and નથી comes in. નથી is is not worn into one word, and it is the same for every person: હું નથી, તે નથી, અમે નથી.
The verb drops its person ending and takes -તો, the shape સમજતો has had all along.
-તો is the man's form. A woman says હું ગુજરાતી નથી બોલતી, with -તી. A group, or a respectful you, take -તા: અમે નથી બોલતા, તમે નથી બોલતા.
નથી may also stand after the verb, as it does in સમજતો નથી. Both orders are everyday Gujarati: હું ગુજરાતી બોલતો નથી says the same thing.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: when there is no other verb

segments.text: With the copula alone, નથી replaces છે and nothing else moves: તે અહીં નથી, she is not here. That was the first job નથી ever did for you.

lessons.title: ન and નહીં — the two smaller nots
lessons.gloss: the two smaller negatives: na before a verb in a request, and nahī̃ for a single word

segments.text: Say I don't drink tea. Then the reply you have given since the first chapters to thanks or to an apology: વાંધો નહીં, no problem. And the word for worry: ચિંતા.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: ન in front of a request

segments.text: નથી denies a statement. A request is not a statement, so it takes the bare ન (na) in front of the verb:
ચિંતા ન કરો. — cintā na karo. — Don't worry.
કરો is the polite do! that માફ કરો has carried since the courtesy chapter. Put ન in front of it and the request becomes a request not to.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: નહીં, for one word

segments.text: નહીં (nahī̃) cancels a word or a phrase rather than a whole sentence:
ચા નહીં, પાણી. — cā nahī̃, pāṇī. — Not tea: water. હમણાં નહીં. — hamṇā̃ nahī̃. — Not now.
વાંધો નહીં is built this way: objection — none.
Three negatives, three jobs:
નથી — a statement: it is not so;
ન — a request: don't;
નહીં — one word: not this.

segments.text: Which negative goes in front of કરો? (ન.) Which one cancels a single word? (નહીં.)

lessons.title: કોઈ નથી — nobody, nothing, never
lessons.gloss: nobody, nothing, never: koī, kaī̃ and kyārey with nathī

segments.text: Say don't worry, then not now. And two words from the chapters on this and that: કોઈ, someone, and કંઈક, something.
અહીં કોઈ નથી. — ahī̃ koī nathī. — There is nobody here.
Gujarati needs no separate word for nobody. It says someone is-not: કોઈ, then નથી.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: કંઈ and ક્યારેય

segments.text: કંઈક is કંઈ with an extra -ક. Before a negative, Gujarati uses the shorter કંઈ (kaī̃):
હું કંઈ નથી ખાતો. — hũ kaī̃ nathī khāto. — I'm not eating anything.
ક્યારેય (kyārey) is ક્યારે, when, with -ય, ever, on the end. With નથી it means never:
તે ક્યારેય ચા નથી પીતી. — te kyārey cā nathī pītī. — She never drinks tea.
The shape is the same three times: an any word, then નથી.

segments.instruction: ahī̃ koī nathī
hũ kaī̃ nathī khāto, or khātī
હું ક્યારેય દૂધ નથી પીતો — hũ kyārey dūdh nathī pīto, I never drink milk
segments.source: [YOU SAY: **હું ક્યારેય દૂધ નથી પીતો** — *hũ kyārey dūdh nathī pīto*, I never drink milk]

segments.text: What does કોઈ નથી say, word for word? (Someone is-not: nobody.) What does -ય add to ક્યારે? (Ever; with નથી, never.) What does કંઈક become before a negative? (કંઈ.)
